text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Judit Csiha, nominee to the post of privatisation minister, said she would accept the post and would begin by reviewing all commission contracts, tenders, and the entire system of file processing.

- Privatisation Minister Tamas Suchman before Parliament's constitutional committee yesterday claimed that he has no legal responsibility over the contract between the State Privatisation and Holding Co. and lawyer Marta Tocsik, as he gave no instructions on the matter, did not tolerate any irregularities, did not approve the HUF 804 million payment to Tocsik and did not know her.

- The cabinet reacted to the Tocsik scandal yesterday by calling for an examination of the asset requirements of local governments. The cabinet also ruled that ministries must immediately examine the use of their funds as well as their practice of calling competitive tenders.
- Romanian President Ion Iliescu signed the Hungarian - Romanian basic treaty into law yesterday.
- Hungary's foreign trade deficit stood at $2 billion in late August, $200 million less than 12 months earlier, said deputy state secretary Lajos Berenyi of the Industry and Trade Ministry.
- Industrial production prices increased by 1.7 percent in August and were 20.9 percent higher than in the same month of 1995, reports the Central Statistics Office.

- Officials of Bayernwerk and RWE/EVS, two German firms that have invested in Hungary's energy sector, yesterday denied reports that they are planning legal action to bring about an energy price increase.

- The Prosecutor General's Office has initiated an investigation into the return to Hungary of Gyorgy Zemplenyi, the former swimming federation president, charged with committing fraud and embezzlement.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Both the Democratic Forum and the Smallholders Party heavily criticised Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze at separate press conferences in connection with the Tocsik scandal.
- Young Democrat President Viktor Orban urged radical changes and a break with the present economic and social policy at a press conference announcing the release of a new policy statement.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Minister of Culture and Education Balint Magyar yesterday outlined measures to overturn a drop in titles published in the past five years.
- The police have amassed a record high debt of HUF 2.5 billion.
- Yesterday's debut of the government's "inflation bond" was a roaring success, attracting HUF 35.8 billion worth of bids for a HUF 8.75 billion issue.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The restriction on cash payments, planned by the government for next year, will not affect the black market but only increase the profits of banks, representatives of the associations of small industrial enterprises and of traders and caterers said.
- The foundation stone will be laid in Mateszalka tomorrow for a factory to produce binoculars for the subsidiary of Germany's Zeiss glass manufacturer.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The fund manager Allied Invest plans to launch a new open-ended fund called A2 within two months.
